entries.name: Sensitivity - Quorum Threshold
entries.purpose: Quorum sweep to characterize decision legitimacy vs throughput.
entries.hypothesis: Increasing quorum has a nonlinear effect on valid proposal completion, with lower completion at thresholds above realized participation.

smallestEffectOfInterest.rationale: A five-percentage-point change in valid completion is governance-relevant and was frozen in the research charter.

entries.experimentalUnit: One seeded DAO simulation replicate under one quorum condition.

outcomes.label: Governance Activity Index
outcomes.unit: turnout-weighted terminal proposals per 100 simulation steps

entries.name: Governance Capture Mitigations
entries.purpose: Sweep vote power mitigations to quantify capture resistance vs throughput.
entries.hypothesis: Vote-power caps and quadratic attenuation reduce the share of proposal-time vote weight controlled by the top token-holding decile while preserving decision throughput.

smallestEffectOfInterest.rationale: A five-percentage-point change in the top token-holding decile's share of cast vote weight is the smallest practically important capture-mitigation effect.

entries.experimentalUnit: One seeded DAO simulation replicate under one factorial policy condition.

entries.name: Proposal Pipeline Effects
entries.purpose: Vary temp-check duration and fast-track rules to assess pipeline impact.
entries.hypothesis: Temp-check and fast-track settings change median time to a valid decision without proportionally increasing abandonment.

smallestEffectOfInterest.rationale: A ten-percent median decision-time change was frozen as the smallest practically important throughput effect.

entries.experimentalUnit: One seeded DAO simulation replicate under one proposal-pipeline condition.

entries.name: Treasury Resilience
entries.purpose: Evaluate treasury stabilization policies under identical governance loads.
entries.hypothesis: Treasury stabilization reduces maximum peak-to-trough treasury drawdown under matched governance load, with effects moderated by explicit protocol yield.

smallestEffectOfInterest.rationale: A five-percentage-point change in maximum peak-to-trough treasury drawdown is the smallest practically important resilience effect.

entries.experimentalUnit: One seeded DAO simulation replicate under one treasury-policy and yield condition.

entries.name: Inter-DAO Cooperation

entries.purpose: Compares governance outcomes across rule-based, hybrid, all-LLM, and hybrid-with-reporter modes using three small LLMs (qwen3:4b, llama3.2:3b, gemma3:4b). Tests whether small models can meaningfully improve governance quality over rule-based agents.

entries.name: Cross-DAO Governance Comparison
entries.purpose: Runs all 14 calibrated DAO digital twins under 4 alternative governance rules (majority, quadratic, conviction, tokenquorum) to identify universal vs DAO-specific governance effects. Each DAO uses its calibrated agent distribution, forum dynamics, and oracle parameters so that governance rule changes are the only independent variable. The grid produces 56 configurations (14 DAOs x 4 rules) enabling both within-DAO and across-DAO comparisons.

entries.name: Black Swan Resilience
entries.purpose: Compares governance mechanism resilience under varying intensities of exogenous shocks (exploits, regulatory events, trust collapses, etc.). Tests whether super-majority or conviction voting provides better stability than simple majority during crises.

entries.name: Counterfactual Governance Expansion (RQ7)
entries.purpose: Comprehensive counterfactual governance analysis across all 14 calibrated DAOs. Tests what happens when each DAO switches to a different governance rule while preserving its calibrated agent dynamics. N=30 runs per configuration for statistical power with confidence intervals.
entries.experimentalUnit: One seeded simulation replicate under one declared condition.

entries.name: Learning Activation Analysis
entries.purpose: Measures the impact of reinforcement learning on agent behavior. Compares fixed heuristics with within-replicate tabular Q-learning, replay, and same-type shared experience. Replicate state is never carried between runs.
entries.hypothesis: Within-replicate tabular learning changes governance activity relative to fixed heuristics, and replay or same-type sharing further changes the learned policy.

smallestEffectOfInterest.rationale: Smaller shifts would not change the substantive interpretation of the primary governance experiments.

entries.experimentalUnit: One independent seeded DAO simulation replicate under one learning condition.
